title: Faster Gradient Methods for Highly-smooth Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
claim: Higher-order variants of our method converge faster and reach better test performance than the first-order baseline and competing methods.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend below, curves colored by method
description: Two side-by-side line plots share a legend placed in a row along the bottom. The left panel shows test loss against iterations from 0 to 1000. The right panel shows test accuracy against iterations over the same range. The legend lists F²SA, F²SA-2, F²SA-3, F²SA-5, F²SA-8, F²SA-10, VRBO, MRBO, stocBiO, and a dashed light-blue line for w/o Reg. In the left panel, the F²SA-p curves drop steeply, and higher p ends lower. Plain F²SA plateaus around 0.73. VRBO, MRBO and stocBiO stay near the dashed no-regularization line at about 0.89. The right panel mirrors this: F²SA-p curves rise to about 0.81–0.82, F²SA stalls near 0.79, and the baselines stay near 0.75. The eye goes first to the spread of colored curves separating from the flat baselines.

abstract: This paper studies the complexity of finding an $Îµ$-stationary point for stochastic bilevel optimization when the upper-level problem is nonconvex and the lower-level problem is strongly convex. Recent work proposed the first-order method, F${}^2$SA, achieving the $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(Îµ^{-6})$ upper complexity bound for first-order smooth problems. This is slower than the optimal $Î©(Îµ^{-4})$ complexity lower bound in its single-level counterpart. In this work, we show that faster rates are achievable for higher-order smooth problems. We first reformulate F$^2$SA as approximating the hyper-gradient with a forward difference. Based on this observation, we propose a class of methods F${}^2$SA-$p$ that uses $p$th-order finite difference for hyper-gradient approximation and improves the upper bound to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(p Îµ^{-4-p/2})$ for $p$th-order smooth problems. Finally, we demonstrate that the $Î©(Îµ^{-4})$ lower bound also holds for stochastic bilevel problems when the high-order smoothness holds for the lower-level variable, indicating that the upper bound of F${}^2$SA-$p$ is nearly optimal in the highly smooth region $p = Î©( \log Îµ^{-1} / \log \log Îµ^{-1})$.
